subject: ss-rheumatology-immunology
title: Cogan syndrome and single organ vasculitis

steps.tx: **Cogan syndrome** is a rare chronic systemic autoimmune disorder and variable-vessel vasculitis characterized by ocular inflammation and sensorineural hearing loss. The disease classically affects young adults, linking non-syphilitic interstitial keratitis with severe, rapidly progressive inner ear audiovestibular dysfunction and vertigo.
steps.say: Cogan syndrome is a systemic variable-vessel vasculitis of young adults. It pairs inflammatory ocular disease with progressive vestibuloauditory impairment.

vis.alt: Clinical features and audiovestibular involvement in Cogan syndrome
vis.caption: Cogan syndrome pairs ocular inflammation with severe audiovestibular dysfunction. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: The definitive clinical hallmark of classic Cogan syndrome is **bilateral non-syphilitic interstitial keratitis** occurring alongside severe **Ménière-like vestibuloauditory dysfunction**. Patients experience acute vertigo, ataxia, nausea, vomiting, tinnitus, and rapidly progressive sensorineural hearing loss that can lead to permanent bilateral deafness within weeks.
steps.say: Classic Cogan syndrome couples bilateral interstitial keratitis with severe Meniere-like vertigo and rapid sensorineural hearing loss that can cause bilateral deafness.

nodes.label: Acute non-syphilitic interstitial keratitis on slit-lamp exam
Ménière-like vertigo, severe ataxia, and high-frequency tinnitus
Rapidly progressive sensorineural hearing loss risking permanent deafness

steps.tx: Atypical Cogan syndrome presents with ocular manifestations other than interstitial keratitis, such as **episcleritis, scleritis, or posterior uveitis**, or audiovestibular symptoms separated in onset by **more than 2 years**. Atypical disease carries a significantly higher frequency of systemic necrotizing vasculitis and vascular complications.
steps.say: Atypical Cogan syndrome presents with scleritis, uveitis, or a delay exceeding two years between eye and ear symptoms. It has higher rates of systemic vasculitis.

left.title: Classic Cogan syndrome
points: Interstitial keratitis within 2 years of vestibuloauditory signs

right.title: Atypical Cogan syndrome
points: Onset interval between eye and ear >2 years
Higher incidence of aortitis and aortic insufficiency

steps.tx: Systemic cardiovascular complications develop in up to **10 to 15 percent** of patients with Cogan syndrome. The most serious vascular lesion is **aortitis**, which causes ascending aortic aneurysmal dilation and severe acute **aortic valve regurgitation**, frequently requiring surgical aortic root replacement.
steps.say: Up to 15 percent of Cogan syndrome patients develop aortitis. Ascending aortic dilation leads to severe aortic regurgitation requiring surgical valve replacement.

rows: Surgical aortic valve and root replacement

steps.tx: **Single-organ vasculitis** or SOV is defined by the Chapel Hill Consensus as necrotizing arteritis or phlebitis strictly limited to a single anatomical organ, lacking systemic features. Prototypic variants comprise **primary angiitis of the central nervous system**, cutaneous leukocytoclastic angiitis, isolated testicular vasculitis, and isolated gastrointestinal arteritis.
steps.say: Single-organ vasculitis is confined to one anatomical organ without systemic involvement. Prototypic examples include primary CNS angiitis and isolated cutaneous vasculitis.

nodes.label: Necrotizing vascular injury verified in solitary organ tissue
Systemic PET-CT, angiograms, and laboratory workup show zero extracranial lesions
Confirmed single-organ vasculitis (PACNS, isolated retinal vasculitis)

steps.tx: **Primary angiitis of the central nervous system** or PACNS is restricted to parenchymal and leptomeningeal arteries under 500 micrometres. Clinical hallmarks include persistent subacute headaches, progressive cognitive decline, and recurrent multifocal ischemic strokes, with definitive diagnosis established by **stereotactic brain-leptomeningeal biopsy**.
steps.say: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system affects small cerebral arteries. Patients present with headaches and strokes, requiring brain biopsy for definitive confirmation.

left.title: PACNS pathology
points: Brain biopsy remains definitive gold standard

right.title: RCVS (Vasculitis mimic)
points: Complete resolution on repeat imaging at 3 months

steps.tx: **Cutaneous single-organ vasculitis** presents with isolated palpable purpura, livedo reticularis, or cutaneous nodules without visceral or renal disease. Histology shows **leukocytoclastic vasculitis** with postcapillary venular fibrinoid necrosis and neutrophil karyorrhexis. Most cases represent self-limiting post-infectious or drug-induced hypersensitivity reactions that resolve with trigger elimination.
steps.say: Cutaneous single-organ vasculitis presents with isolated palpable purpura. Biopsy shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis with fibrinoid necrosis and neutrophil nuclear debris.

steps.tx: Therapy for acute audiovestibular dysfunction in Cogan syndrome demands immediate **high-dose systemic glucocorticoids** with oral prednisone at 1 mg/kg/day or IV pulse methylprednisolone. For refractory inner ear sensorineural loss, TNF inhibitors such as **infliximab** or tocilizumab preserve hearing; patients with profound bilateral deafness benefit significantly from **cochlear implantation**.
steps.say: Acute hearing loss in Cogan syndrome mandates immediate high-dose glucocorticoids. Infliximab controls refractory inflammation, while cochlear implants restore hearing in deafness.

nodes.label: Immediate pulse methylprednisolone within 2 weeks of hearing onset
Early escalation to infliximab or tocilizumab for refractory deafness
Cochlear implantation for permanent profound bilateral sensorineural loss
